resources.string:
A local VPN is created on this device. All network traffic passes through it so the app can show which apps talk to whom. Nothing is ever sent to the makers of CoreLock.
What does leave this phone:
• Your DNS lookups, to the resolver you choose in Settings (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 by default; encrypted to cloudflare-dns.com, dns.google or dns.quad9.net only when you turn on DoH).
• Blocklist downloads, about once a week: the HaGeZi lists from raw.githubusercontent.com (or cdn.jsdelivr.net when GitHub cannot be reached) and the OISD list from small.oisd.nl.
• The Exodus tracker list, at most once a week: reports.exodus-privacy.eu.org.
Only if you turn them on in Settings:
• Certificate Transparency checks: the domains you visit are sent to crt.sh.
• The public IP check in Diagnostics: asks api.ipify.org.

Traffic logs are stored encrypted in the app’s private storage on this device. They are never uploaded. They leave the phone only when you share an export yourself (PCAP, CSV or IT report). You can delete them at any time from Settings.
It blocks ads, trackers and malware on this phone.
Nothing leaves your phone for us: your history stays here, encrypted.
It can\'t block ads inside YouTube, Instagram, Snapchat, TikTok or Facebook.
Why Android asks about a VPN
CoreLock uses Android\'s VPN feature to check connections on your phone. Your traffic isn\'t sent to us: we have no servers.
Android asks you once to allow it.
You can change this at any time on Home.
Android limits CoreLock in the background, so protection may stop. Allow it to run in the background.
